History and Physical (Super Detailed)

Consult Summary:
23-year-old woman with a 3–4-day history of constant, worsening midline lower-abdominal pain (8/10) associated with light post-menstrual vaginal bleeding and mild nausea; advised urgent face-to-face abdominal exam and repeat pregnancy test today.

History:
• Presenting complaint – Constant lower-abdominal pain  
  – Location: midline, below the umbilicus  
  – Onset: “few days ago”; has progressively worsened  
  – Severity: 8/10  
  – Character: constant; no reported radiation  
• Associated symptoms  
  – Light pink vaginal bleeding occurring after normal period ended ~2 weeks ago  
  – Mild nausea without vomiting  
  – Constipation for one week last week, now resolved; current stools normal  
  – Slight vaginal discharge (no malodor noted)  
  – Denies fever, shoulder pain, shortness of breath, dizziness/faintness, urinary frequency/urgency/dysuria, visible hematuria, diarrhea, or weight loss  
• Menstrual/gynecologic history  
  – Last menstrual period: ~2–3 weeks ago, described as normal  
  – Cycles irregular since insertion of etonogestrel implant one year ago  
  – Sexual activity: sexually active; intercourse 4 days ago  
  – Contraception: etonogestrel implant (“Implanon”) in situ ×1 year  
  – Pregnancy test: negative ~1 month ago; none since pain onset  
• Functional status: able to work, cook, and perform usual activities though discomfort is significant during pain episodes  
• Systems review: all other systems not specifically noted above – no additional complaints elicited

Past Medical History:
• Medication allergy: Amoxicillin – “allergic”; reaction details not documented  
• No chronic medical conditions reported  
• No prior surgeries  
• No previous pregnancies

Medications:
• Etonogestrel implant (Implanon) – dose/route/frequency not documented  
• No other regular medications mentioned

Social History:
• Occupation: school teacher  
• Living situation: lives with husband and husband’s family  
• Smoking: denies  
• Alcohol: unclear – patient response “I don’t know” (conflict noted)  
• Recreational drugs: denies  
• Travel: abroad approximately one year ago, none recent

Family History:
• Not discussed / not documented

Physical Examination:
• Not performed in this tele-consultation

Investigations:
• Home urine pregnancy test – negative one month ago (before current symptoms)  
• No other labs or imaging performed

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1: Acute lower-abdominal pain with light post-menstrual bleeding, possible gynecologic or gastrointestinal etiology (rule out early pregnancy/ectopic, pelvic infection, ovarian pathology, bowel disorder).  
  – Arrange urgent face-to-face appointment for abdominal and, if indicated, pelvic examination.  
  – Repeat urine pregnancy test today; if positive, patient to contact service immediately.  
  – Advise patient to call support line to schedule clinic assessment.  
  – Counsel on red-flag/worsening symptoms: escalating pain, inability to tolerate oral fluids, fever, syncope, or positive pregnancy test → seek urgent care.

Issue 2: Contraception follow-up (etonogestrel implant).  
  – Confirm implant status and continue use if no complications identified during upcoming exam.  
  – Review menstrual irregularities in context of implant at face-to-face visit.

Issue 3: Recent constipation (now resolved).  
  – No active treatment required; encourage adequate hydration and dietary fiber.

General plan items:  
• Provide visit details and safety-net advice as above.  
• No prescriptions issued during this call.

Quality checks:

Missing but clinically expected elements:  
• Complete medication list (only implant documented).  
• Detailed allergy reaction description.  
• Vital signs and physical examination findings.  
• Full gynecologic history (e.g., cervical screening status).  
• Comprehensive family history.

Internal conflicts:  
• Alcohol intake uncertain – patient responded “I don’t know.”  
• No other conflicts noted.

Transcript quality: several inaudible or clipped segments; however, main clinical information obtainable.
